genesis.50.p1.b1.text: Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.

genesis.50.p1.b2.text: And Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel.

genesis.50.p1.b3.text: taking the forty days required to complete the embalming. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.

genesis.50.p2.b1.text: If I have found favor in your eyes, please tell Pharaoh that

genesis.50.p2.b2.text: my father made me swear an oath when he said, ‘I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’

genesis.50.p2.b3.text: Now let me go and bury my father, and then return.

genesis.50.p2.b4.text: Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.

genesis.50.p3.b1.text: Then Joseph went to bury his father, and all the servants of Pharaoh accompanied him—the elders of Pharaoh’s household and all the elders of the land of Egypt—

genesis.50.p3.b2.text: along with all of Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and his father’s household.

genesis.50.p3.b3.text: Chariots and horsemen alike went up with him, and it was an exceedingly large procession.

genesis.50.p4.b1.text: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, they lamented and wailed loudly, and Joseph mourned for his father seven days.

genesis.50.p4.b2.text: This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.

genesis.50.p4.b3.text: So Jacob’s sons did as he had charged them. They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre,

genesis.50.p4.b4.text: After Joseph had buried his father, he returned to Egypt with his brothers and all who had gone with him to bury his father.

genesis.50.p5.b1.text: What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.

genesis.50.p5.b2.text: Before he died, your father commanded, … I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.

genesis.50.p5.b3.text: When their message came to him, Joseph wept.

genesis.50.p6.b1.text: Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?

genesis.50.p6.b2.text: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this—to preserve the lives of many people.

genesis.50.p6.b4.text: So Joseph reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them.

genesis.50.p7.b1.text: Now Joseph and his father’s household remained in Egypt, and Joseph lived to the age of 110. … the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees.

genesis.50.p7.b2.text: I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

genesis.50.p7.b3.text: God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.

genesis.50.p7.b4.text: So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.
